briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Cannabis Steadies as Federal Tailwinds Build
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market is finding its footing after the 24% wholesale tax shock, with sales stabilizing, new stores opening, and a gubernatorial candidate now courting the industry with a repeal pledge. Nationally, courts just kept cannabis at Schedule III, Big Pharma is pouring billions into psychedelics, and MSOs are chasing cross-border deals — real momentum for operators to plan around.

local.text: House of Dank opens 12th Michigan store in Ann Arbor — the Detroit-born chain is opening its 12th House of Dank location in Ann Arbor at 2730 Jackson Ave.

Michigan cannabis sales top $17 billion since launch — Michigan has surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales since regulated sales began, with August generating approximately $259.09 million, pushing cumulative adult-use sales above $15.41 billion and medical sales above $1.63 billion.
Sales stabilize months after the 24% wholesale tax hit — by March, sales had climbed back to $255.4 million and held relatively steady through June at $253.5 million, per Headset data.

GOP nominee vows to kill the wholesale tax — Republican John James is proposing to "repeal or sharply reduce" Michigan's new 24% wholesale tax on marijuana and courting industry donors as he competes to be Michigan's next governor.

Jars Cannabis wins surveillance-camera fight in Madison Heights — the retail chain reached an agreement with city authorities to remove a Flock surveillance camera aimed at the store's parking lot entrance, and the camera came down pending City Council approval.

national.text: Court keeps medical cannabis locked in at Schedule III — the D.C. Circuit Court declined to stay the rescheduling of medical marijuana, meaning it will remain Schedule III while a lawsuit from anti-marijuana groups proceeds.

Compass Pathways closes in on an FDA decision — the company is in the midst of a rolling submission to the FDA for its psilocybin candidate COMP360, with analysts anticipating a possible approval by year end.
Eli Lilly bets big on psychedelics — the pharma giant provided "the ultimate validation for the space this summer with the $3.8 billion acquisition of AtaiBeckley".

Curaleaf chases cross-border MSO merger with Aurora — Curaleaf's US$4-per-share takeover bid, a 45% premium creating $1.5 billion-plus in pro forma revenue, signals major MSOs are now thinking cross-border.

Psychedelic sector pushes forward past Lykos shakeup — Lykos Therapeutics' CEO Amy Emerson stepped down following the FDA's MDMA rejection, but Compass Pathways and Definium Therapeutics are now leading the next wave of filings.
